latest_release.name: Speckled Clarkia
latest_release.body:
iMessage Exporter 5.0.1: [Speckled Clarkia](https://calscape.org/plant/1034/Clarkia-cylindrica-ssp.-cylindrica-(Speckled-Clarkia)) contains the following fixes and improvements:

- New Features
  - Contacts-based conversation merging
    - Combine phone numbers and email addresses belonging to one person, including linked Contacts cards on macOS and iOS
    - Merge conversations split across those addresses, including group chats
    - Preserve separate group chats with different names unless Messages explicitly links them
    - Skip ambiguous identity matches when an address belongs to multiple Contacts cards
  - Allow `--contacts-path` (`-n`) to override the Contacts database in encrypted and unencrypted iOS backups
- Performance
  - Read message bodies and edit histories with message rows instead of fetching them separately for each message
  - Parse body data directly from query results, avoiding intermediate buffers in the main decoding path
  - Replace the separate payload-presence query with a flag in the message query
- Bug Fixes
  - Fix inflated poll vote counts when participants change selections or Messages repeats vote updates for #823
  - Fix null values in archived app-message payloads and render links as plain URLs when preview metadata is absent or null for #805
  - Preserve recovered body components and edit history when text recovery fails
  - Keep attachments and handwriting from recovered deleted messages in their conversation’s attachment directory for #827
  - Route messages from linked chat rows without participant records to their conversation instead of the orphaned transcript
  - Fix incorrect contact matches caused by country-code collisions and iOS search-index phone fragments
  - Reject unmatched conversation filters even when date filters are supplied
  - Reject out-of-range handwriting dimensions and handle empty text-rendering canvases
  - Fix a performance regression where the bundled SQLite 3.54 update recompiled cached queries for every message for #839
- Enhancements
  - Improve conversation naming and filtering
    - Use one filename and attachment directory for every chat row in a merged conversation
    - Choose consistent contact names and fallback addresses, honoring linked contacts’ preferred names
    - List each participant once and improve long filename truncation and remaining-participant counts
    - Match conversation filters against every Messages address belonging to a grouped participant
  - Clarify diagnostic counts and report participants and conversations merged through Contacts
  - Improve database and backup path errors for #829, #808, #647, #590, #493, and #359
    - Distinguish missing paths, permission failures, invalid SQLite files, and databases without Messages data
    - Suggest database and backup locations based on files found on disk
    - Improve default home-directory resolution, including Windows support
- API Changes
  - Breaking ([migration guide](https://github.com/ReagentX/imessage-exporter/tree/develop/docs/migration/speckled-clarkia))
    - Decode message text, body components, and edit history during row loading; remove separate body-decoding calls
    - Replace callback streaming and generic query/cache traits with prepared-statement iteration and concrete APIs
    - Separate participant identity groups from stored addresses and use those groups for chat deduplication
    - Return decoded timestamps in UTC and accept explicit timezones for date filtering and presentation
    - Separate exported attachment paths and media types from database rows
    - Revise diagnostic fields, error variants, and public module paths
  - Ergonomic
    - Re-export `chrono`, `plist`, and `rusqlite` from `imessage_database`
- Miscellaneous
  - Exclude test fixtures from the published library package
  - Recommend `cargo install --locked`
  - Expand regression coverage, consolidate exporter tests, and enforce formatting in CI

detail.readme:
# imessage-exporter

This crate provides both a library to interact with iMessage data as well as a binary that can perform some useful read-only operations using that data. The aim of this project is to provide the most comprehensive and accurate representation of iMessage data available.

This free and open-source software can:

- Save, export, backup, and archive iMessage data to open, portable formats
- Preserve multimedia content (images, videos, audio) from conversations
- Facilitate easy migration of message history between devices and platforms
- Run diagnostics on the iMessage database
- Give you full ownership and control over your communication history
- Support compliance with data retention policies or legal requirements
- Run on macOS, Linux, and Windows

## Example Export

![HTML Export Sample](/docs/hero.png)

## Binary

The `imessage-exporter` binary exports iMessage data to `txt` or `html` formats. It can also run diagnostics to find problems with the iMessage database.

Installation instructions for the binary are located [here](imessage-exporter/README.md).

## Library

The `imessage_database` library provides models that allow us to access iMessage information as native, cross-platform data structures.

Documentation for the library is located [here](imessage-database/README.md).

### Supported Features

Support for every iMessage feature as of macOS Golden Gate 27.2 (26B123) and iOS 27.2 (24B119):

- iMessage, RCS, SMS, and MMS
- Multi-part messages
- Replies/Threads
- Formatted text
- Attachments
- Expressives
- Tapbacks
- Stickers
- Apple Pay
- Group chats
- Digital Touch
- URL Previews
- Audio messages
- App Integrations
- Edited messages
- Business messages
- Handwritten messages

See more detail about supported features [here](docs/features.md).

## Frequently Asked Questions

The FAQ document is located [here](/docs/faq.md).

## Special Thanks

- All of my friends, for putting up with me sending them random messages to test things
- [SQLiteFlow](https://www.sqliteflow.com), the SQL viewer I used to explore and reverse engineer the iMessage database
- [Xplist](https://github.com/ic005k/Xplist), an invaluable tool for reverse engineering the `payload_data` plist format
- [Compart](https://www.compart.com/en/unicode/), an amazing resource for looking up esoteric unicode details
- [GNU Project](https://github.com/gnustep/libobjc) and [Archive.org](https://archive.org/details/darwin_0.1), for hosting source code referenced to reverse engineer the `typedstream` format
